comment: compass v1.2 · outreach quality anchor pack · for personalized email/X/dev.to/github outreach drafts. Used by publisher.drift_check gate before send. Goal: prevent spam/template/over-claim drift when agent autonomy increases (V7 / nautilus-prime-001 raid auto-publish). 25 positive + 35 negative anchors.
loaded_by: publisher when message_kind in (outreach-email, outreach-reply, outreach-followup, outreach-x-reply)
positive_anchors: references a specific sentence, figure, or method from the recipient's actual work
names a concrete connection between our work and theirs · not generic praise
offers a low-friction first step · the recipient can ack with 5 minutes of effort
respects the recipient's time · explicitly acknowledges their constraints
phased ramp · the ask scales only with what's already been learned
honest about limitations · says 'kill it cheaply' or 'null result is publishable'
specific to one person · the email body cannot be substituted to a different recipient
links to verifiable artifact · arxiv ID / GitHub URL / HF dataset URL · not vague claims
asks one clear question · not three vague ones
tone is peer-to-peer not vendor pitch · no marketing copy
subject line is concrete · names the connection rather than the offer
body length appropriate to ask · short ask = short email · big ask = explain
no over-claims about own work · uses numbers with caveats and uncertainty
credits prior work fairly · including direct competitors when relevant
thanks for the introduction or onboarding if applicable · no fake hype
agreed-to follow-up arrives when promised · or explicit notice when delayed
reply matches the depth of the inbound · short ack to short msg · detail to detail
if rejecting collaboration · explains why and suggests alternative
signs with real name and clear affiliation · not anonymous
if cold outreach · explicitly states how I found the recipient
mentions specific data point or metric from their work to prove I read it
offers a Colab / runnable demo as the lowest-friction step
explicit timezone and async-ok statement when relevant
doesn't ask for endorsement / introduction within the first email
the ask is proportional to the value offered · not asymmetric extraction
negative_anchors: generic template with name substituted · could be sent to anyone in the field
asks for the recipient's time without offering anything concrete in return
subject line is 'collaboration opportunity' or 'quick question'
uses revolutionary / game-changing / paradigm-shifting / breakthrough language
claims industry SOTA or undisputed leader without verifiable comparison
many emojis · multiple exclamation marks · urgent CTA
no specific reference to recipient's work · just praise their 'amazing research'
asks for endorsement / referral / introduction in cold first email
long opening preamble before the actual ask
offers free product trial as if recipient hasn't seen 100 of those this month
asks the recipient to fix a bug in our work · disguised as collaboration
uses 'we' when there is only one person on our side · false bigness
exaggerates own benchmark numbers · drops caveats
dismisses competitors with 'they are dead' / 'they failed' rhetoric without evidence
claims compass is the only solution for X · ignores valid alternatives
no plan for what happens after the recipient replies · waste their effort
spam keywords trigger · 'limited time' · 'act now' · 'don't miss out'
AI-written tells · 'I hope this email finds you well' opening
lists 10 features when 2 would suffice · feature dump
asks recipient to debate methodology without first acknowledging their evidence
long signature with multiple titles · credential stuffing
follow-up email arrives within 24 hours of the first · pressure tactic
follow-up doesn't reference the original · feels like a fresh cold email
more than 3 followups on the same thread without new information
guilt-trip language · 'I notice you haven't replied' · 'just bumping this up'
uses recipient's first name 5+ times in a short email · fake intimacy
claims a connection that doesn't exist · 'we met at NeurIPS' when we didn't
asks recipient to publicly endorse our work via tweet / blog / review
passive-aggressive framing · 'I'm sure you're too busy to respond'
comparison-shaming · 'unlike X who is closed-source, we are open'
implies recipient is missing out · FOMO manipulation
asks for paid collaboration / equity / advisory role in cold first contact
uses recipient's institution name as flattery · 'researchers at <prestigious>'
drops a famous researcher's name without consent or context · name-dropping
ignores recipient's stated preference in their bio · e.g. 'no cold pitches'
